newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY'S WHEAT FUTURES FALL TRACKING CHICAGO.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY'S WHEAT FUTURES FALL TRACKING CHICAGO.

text.p: Hungary's wheat futures eased by the daily limit of 400 forints in brisk trading on Wednesday due to price falls on the international markets and because some market players believed the weather was good to the crop, traders said.
"Prices in Chicago went down by 10 to 14 cents per bushel overnight and we followed it," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap Ugynoki Kft.
"And the rainy, moist weather is good for the crop," he added, quoting the Hungarian proverb "rain in May equals gold."

However, other market players believed the weather is too rainy and may beat down the crop, and the differential between opinions helped boost the Budapest Commodity Exchange's (BCE) grains futures turnover to 1.04 billion forints from the usual levels of a few hundred million.
Traders said wheat futures were likely to drop further on Thursday, reflecting Wednesday's slowing price falls in Chicago.
Maize futures closed mixed as deals just before closing pushed up the prices of some maturities.
Usually tradeless blackseed futures saw heavy trade on Wednesday, with the November maturity accounting for 223 lots of the total grains turnover of 2,047 lots.
Traders could not explain this high turnover, but some of them tought it unlikely that actual deliveries were behind the deal.
